title: Solving Linear Inequalities in One Variable
student_objective: I can solve one-variable linear inequalities, reverse the inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative number, represent solutions, and justify each step.
teacher_objective: Diagnose inequality-solving misconceptions at the first incorrect step, especially failure to reverse the inequality after multiplying or dividing by a negative number, and route students to targeted remediation.

concept_cards.title: An inequality describes a set of values
concept_cards.content: An inequality usually describes many values that make a comparison true.

concept_cards.title: Keep equivalent inequalities
concept_cards.content: Adding or subtracting the same quantity on both sides preserves the inequality. Multiplying or dividing both sides by the same positive quantity also preserves its direction.

concept_cards.title: Reverse for a negative multiplier or divisor
concept_cards.content: When both sides are multiplied or divided by a negative number, reverse the inequality symbol. For example, -2x > 6 becomes x < -3.

concept_cards.title: Check a solution value
concept_cards.content: Choose a value from the proposed solution set and substitute it into the original inequality.

concept_cards.title: Represent the solution
concept_cards.content: Use an open endpoint for < or > and a closed endpoint for ≤ or ≥, then shade toward all values that satisfy the inequality.

items.tutor_behavior: Review subtraction on both sides while preserving the comparison.

Add 4, divide by positive 3, then verify the boundary value.

items.tutor_behavior: Emphasize the reversal at the negative division step.

items.prompt: Solve 6x + 1 ≥ 25. Give your first step before finishing.
items.tutor_behavior: Ask which operation to undo first.
Distribute first, then ask whether the final negative division requires reversing the symbol.

items.prompt: A student solves -5x > 20 and writes x > -4. Give the correct solution.
items.explanation_prompt: Explain the student's mistake and why the inequality direction changes.
items.explanation_guidance: State that dividing both sides by a negative number reverses the inequality direction.
items.tutor_behavior: Require the student to state why division by -5 reverses the inequality.
Undo subtraction, then divide by a positive coefficient.
Diagnose whether the inequality reverses during negative division.
Track the final division by -2 and the required reversal.

Diagnose distribution and variables-on-both-sides errors separately.

items.prompt: A student changes 4x < 12 to x > 3. Give the correct solution.
items.tutor_behavior: Explain that division by a positive number preserves direction.

items.prompt: Which graph represents x > -2? Answer: open right, open left, closed right, or closed left.
items.tutor_behavior: Separate endpoint openness from shading direction.

items.prompt: Which graph represents x ≤ 4? Answer: open right, open left, closed right, or closed left.
items.tutor_behavior: Connect ≤ with a closed endpoint and values left of 4.

items.prompt: A number line has an open circle at 6 and is shaded left. Write the inequality.
items.tutor_behavior: Translate endpoint type and shading direction independently.

items.prompt: A number line has a closed circle at -1 and is shaded right. Write the inequality.
items.tutor_behavior: Translate a closed endpoint and rightward ray into symbolic form.
Check reversal even when both numbers are negative.
Distribute and collect terms without changing the inequality direction.

items.prompt: Is x = 2 included in the solution x < 2? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Connect a strict symbol to an open endpoint and excluded boundary.

items.prompt: Is x = -3 included in the solution x ≥ -3? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Connect ≥ to a closed endpoint and included boundary.
